report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/eval/tasks.py: module docstring + resolve_task_repo, is_correctness_task, task_project_label, TASKS prefix. Claims about repo resolution, correctness-key detection, unknown-repo labeling, and task labels verified; some reachability claims uncheckable.
risks: tasks.py:18 | medium | 'must_include' labels verified reachable by running semantic_slice (circular claim) — cannot be verified from this chunk; requires harness/slicer execution.
tasks.py:80 | low | resolve_task_repo falls back to resolve_repo_root(None, repo) for registered projects; exact behavior of that function is outside this chunk.

tasks.py:97 | low | is_correctness_task keys on presence of fail_to_pass/pass_to_pass; a malformed task with 'fail_to_pass': [] is treated as correctness (intended per docstring) but validation happens in correctness.validate_task, not here.
tasks.py:123 | low | task_project_label returns repo string for unknown labels; project filtering semantics in harness are outside this chunk.
tasks.py:145-220 | medium | Every task's must_include/answer_contains claims about real dependencies are uncheckable from this chunk; they reference code in other files.
tasks.py:191-197 | medium | Comment claims semantic_slice no longer uses _py_maps and now uses _reverse_edges; that is a claim about another file's internals, uncheckable here.

handoff.purpose: Defines the eval task corpus and the predicates that distinguish slice-recall tasks from correctness tasks; begins the TASKS list.

symbols.name: AGENT_ENV_ROOT
symbols.note: str, parents[2] of this file; used by resolve_task_repo for the 'agent_env' label.

symbols.name: resolve_task_repo
symbols.note: Maps repo label to absolute path: 'agent_env' -> AGENT_ENV_ROOT; absolute existing path -> as-is; registered name -> resolve_repo_root(None, repo); else ValueError.

symbols.name: CORRECTNESS_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple ('fail_to_pass', 'pass_to_pass'); presence of either marks a task as correctness-format.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: True iff task is a dict and any correctness key is present (presence, not truthiness).

symbols.name: task_project_label
symbols.note: Returns '<unknown>' when repo key absent; 'agent_env' for the label or root; otherwise the repo value.

symbols.name: TASKS
symbols.note: List[dict]; first 11 slice-recall tasks (file-level and symbol-level) with must_include labels, all hand_reachable/primary.

claims.text: Each task targets a real symbol/file in a small repo and records the symbols a *sufficient* distilled slice MUST carry to reason about that target.
claims.why: The task dicts list must_include symbols, but whether those symbols are truly sufficient cannot be verified from this chunk; it depends on the slicer and other files.

claims.text: a label is only listed if a competent answer about the target genuinely needs it AND it is a real dependency or caller in the neighborhood.
claims.why: Requires knowledge of the target code and dependency graphs; not derivable from this chunk.

claims.text: For a symbol target the slice is 1-hop (the focus symbol's direct callees/callers), so we only label symbols reachable within that hop -- we do NOT claim transitive callees-of-callees are present when they are not.
claims.why: Describes slicing behavior implemented in daedalus.eval.harness/semantic_slice; not observable here.

claims.text: Every task below is this provenance today. Recall computed over ``hand_reachable`` tasks is an upper bound / sanity check, NOT independent proof the slicer works -- ``report.py`` says so on every render, and ``harness.run_tier1`` never blends it with the other provenances into one number.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable', but the behavior of report.py and harness.run_tier1 is outside this chunk.

claims.text: ``tier``: "primary" tasks count toward any go/no-go recall number. "quarantine" tasks are minted but not yet confirmed -- ``harness.run_tier1`` excludes them from every headline/aggregate and reports them separately
claims.why: The tier semantics are enforced in harness.run_tier1; not visible here. All tasks in this chunk are 'primary', so the quarantine behavior is not exercised.

claims.text: a correctness task carries no ``must_include``, so scoring one with ``harness._recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0 -- a task that cannot fail, silently inflating the very number the tier machinery exists to keep honest.
claims.why: harness._recall behavior is not in this chunk; the claim about vacuous 1.0 depends on that implementation.

claims.text: ``is_correctness_task`` below is the single predicate that decides, and ``harness.eval_task_tier1``/``eval_task_arms`` refuse such a task loudly (an ERRORED row, which ``run_gate`` reports and fails on for a primary tier) instead of grading it.
claims.why: The refusal behavior is in harness.eval_task_tier1/eval_task_arms/run_gate; not visible here. The predicate itself is verified below.

claims.text: Correctness tasks live in their own store (``correctness.DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH``) and never enter ``harness.all_tasks()``.
claims.why: References correctness module and harness.all_tasks(); not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: agent_env repo root == parents[2] of this file (daedalus/eval/tasks.py).
claims.why: AGENT_ENV_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]); given the file path daedalus/eval/tasks.py, parents[2] is the repo root.

claims.text: "agent_env" -> this harness repo (dogfood target)
claims.why: if repo == 'agent_env': return AGENT_ENV_ROOT; AGENT_ENV_ROOT is defined as the repo root.

claims.text: a registered name -> daedalus.projects.resolve_repo_root (e.g. sunny_garden)
claims.why: if repo in list_projects(): return resolve_repo_root(None, repo); resolve_repo_root is imported from daedalus.projects.

claims.text: an absolute path -> used as-is (temp fixtures in tests)
claims.why: if os.path.isabs(repo) and Path(repo).exists(): return repo; the path is returned unchanged.

claims.text: Deliberately keyed on the PRESENCE of the field, not on its truthiness: a task with "fail_to_pass": [] is a correctness task with an empty (and therefore invalid, see correctness.validate_task) test list, NOT a slice-recall task
claims.why: The function uses 'any(k in task for k in CORRECTNESS_KEYS)', which checks presence (key membership), not truthiness.

claims.text: it must never be handed to _recall, which would score its absent must_include as a vacuous 1.0. That is the exact shape of the failure this predicate exists to make impossible.
claims.why: The behavior of _recall is in harness; not visible here. The predicate itself does prevent such tasks from being identified as slice-recall, but the claim about _recall's scoring is external.

claims.text: A task with NO ``repo`` key labels as ``"<unknown>"`` rather than raising ``KeyError``.
claims.why: Uses task.get('repo'); if repo is None, returns '<unknown>'.

claims.text: this function is called from ``harness._task_error_row``, i.e. on the REPORTING path for a task that is already known to be malformed, so a raise here turned "one bad task is reported as a degraded row" into "the whole eval run dies on it" -- the exact failure ``_task_error_row`` exists to prevent.
claims.why: The call site in harness._task_error_row is not in this chunk.

claims.text: All Tier-1 labels verified reachable against the current slices -- which is exactly the circularity documented above. Every task is "hand_reachable" / "primary" until an "independent_diff" or "temporal_churn" minter (see daedalus.eval.mint, a separate track) adds tasks with independent labels.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable' and tier 'primary'; no other provenance or tier appears.

observations.what: The module docstring makes many claims about harness, correctness, slicer, and report behavior that are not present in this chunk; they are all uncheckable here.
All tasks in this chunk are 'hand_reachable'/'primary', matching the comment that no independent_diff/temporal_churn tasks exist yet.

resolve_task_repo's absolute-path branch requires Path(repo).exists(); a non-existent absolute path falls through to list_projects() check and then raises ValueError. This matches the docstring 'used as-is (temp fixtures in tests)' only for existing paths.
task_project_label returns the raw repo string for any repo that is not None and not agent_env/AGENT_ENV_ROOT, including absolute paths. This is the intended bucket for --project filtering.
